title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC0RE_1LE1LD_1RE0LC_1RA1RA_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC0RE_1LE1LD_1RE0LC_1RA1RA_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A two-level counter: blocks of 2 at the right end grow by one per round in doubling time while an 11 walks left through a list of 5s; rebuilt at 2e5, 1.1e7, 1.8e8 steps; open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 287 cells have been visited and 213 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in A on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps; rebuilds
claims.text: Direct simulation. The fast counter is the run of blocks of length 2 at the right end, after the last 8: it grows by one block in every round, and each round takes about twice as long as the one before (T′ = 2T + 9 in the regular stretches). The slow list was rebuilt at about 2.0·10<sup>5</sup>, 1.06·10<sup>7</sup> and 1.78·10<sup>8</sup> steps; between rebuilds each round makes one local change in it.

claims.title: Two-level counter
claims.text: Left of it the slow list is made of blocks of length 2 mod 3 (5, 8, 11, 17, …) behind a fixed head 6 2 6. In each round one walker, an 11, moves one block to the left through the 5s (5 11 → 11 5), sometimes merging (8 11 → … 14); when it reaches the head of the list the list is rebuilt: the 2s of the fast counter are absorbed into new 5s and a new walk starts with more blocks to cross. Not shown for all sizes.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. See the heuristic claims above for what a halt would need.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_1RC0LF_1RD1RD_1RE1RA_1LF0RC_1LC1LB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a two-level counter: a fast counter at the right end of the tape needs twice as long for each round, and each round makes one small change in a slow list of blocks on its left; rarely the slow list is rebuilt. This page runs the machine and shows the rounds.

facts.text: Rounds of the run proved in Lean for any tape further left.
Each round twice as long as the one before.

sections.heading: A fast counter and a slow list
html: Look at the tape each time the head is in state A on the first blank cell right of everything written. The tape is then blocks of 1s separated by single 0s (5^4 is four blocks of length 5, … an unchanged stretch). The fast counter is the run of blocks of length 2 at the right end, after the last 8: it grows by one block in every round, and each round takes about twice as long as the one before (T′ = 2T + 9 in the regular stretches).

Left of it the slow list is made of blocks of length 2 mod 3 (5, 8, 11, 17, …) behind a fixed head 6 2 6. In each round one walker, an 11, moves one block to the left through the 5s (5 11 → 11 5), sometimes merging (8 11 → … 14); when it reaches the head of the list the list is rebuilt: the 2s of the fast counter are absorbed into new 5s and a new walk starts with more blocks to cross.

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine can halt only on its one undefined transition. The regular rounds are proved in Lean for three instances (for every tape further left) and behave the same way in every round seen; a halt could only come from a rebuild of the slow list (seen at about 2.0·105, 1.06·107 and 1.78·108 steps). Rebuilds come after exponentially many rounds, and their rule is not known for all sizes, so the run cannot be followed beyond direct simulation. Since every rebuild seen made the list longer, the machine looks like it runs forever, but that is an extrapolation.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.073).
After 109 steps the tape spans 287 cells (50 left of the start, 233 right), with a density of 1s of 0.742.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
